subject: Re: Redwood Private/VPC pricing - token volumes & licensing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood Private/VPC pricing - post-call recap & next steps

Alex — great to connect earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can put together a draft pricing SOW for FinTechCo: 

1) What we heard on the call
- You’re interested in Redwood Private (VPC) to keep inference traffic inside your cloud and integrate with your KMS for keying.
- Current inference volume: ~100M tokens/month today, with a plan to grow to ~300M tokens/month within 12 months.
- Need 24/7 enterprise support and a private control plane.
- Environments: prod + dev, and a DR/standby region.

2) Concrete asks from our side to price accurately
- Confirm the token volume buckets you expect for month 1 and month 12 (if the 300M is month-12).
- Target unit economics: you mentioned a target of roughly $/1M tokens — can you confirm the target range you'd be comfortable with?
- Expected concurrency / peak qps and typical sequence length (avg tokens per request).
- Preferred licensing model: per-environment licensing (flat license + support) vs committed throughput (tokens/month reservation) — do you have a preference?

3) Next steps
- If you can share a short token extract or a monthly token CSV we’ll use it to run unit-cost estimates (compute + storage + support).
- We’ll draft a preliminary pricing SOW and rough $/1M token bands for both (a) license + per-instance pricing and (b) committed tokens model.
- Proposed follow-up: 30 min on Mon 2026-10-05 to walk through numbers and align on model.

Attaching a short overview of Redwood Private for context.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-private-pricing-overview.pdf (1 page stub)

From: Alex Johnson <alex@fintechco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Private/VPC pricing - post-call recap & next steps

Ben — thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token volumes: 100M tokens/month today (October baseline). We expect roughly 2-3x growth in the next 6-12 months; planning for 300M tokens/month by Oct 2027 is safe. For initial pricing please model both 100M and 300M scenarios.
- Target $/1M tokens: our finance team has penciled a target of about $450 per 1M tokens for a fully-managed private option (includes licensing and enterprise support) — we understand that’s aggressive but wanted to state the budget range. 
- Licensing model: preference is towards a committed throughput model (tokens/month reservation) with a premium for enterprise support and a small per-instance license for the VPC control plane. Open to alternatives if you can show unit cost benefits.
- Environments: Prod + Dev + DR (DR in a second region). So effectively 3 environments.
- Support: Enterprise 24/7 with a 1-hour P1 SLA.

I attached a quick token export for Q3 so you can get a rough distribution. Happy to take the 10/5 call — Mon 10/05 at 10:00am PT works for me.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of ML Engineering, FinTechCo
alex@fintechco.com
Attachment: fintech_token_report_q3.csv (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T18:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Private/VPC pricing - post-call recap & next steps

Alex — perfect, this is super helpful. A few quick clarifications so our pricing draft matches your assumptions: 

- When you say $450 / 1M tokens, do you mean inference tokens only (prompt + completion) as reported by your usage extraction? That’s how we typically model committed throughput.
- For the committed model we’ll show a step-down per-1M token price as volume increases (100M, 300M, 1B). For the license + per-instance model we’ll show a baseline private license + per-GPU seat pricing and expected monthly ops cost.
- For environments we’ll model 3 separate environments, but we typically allow shared control-plane licensing with per-environment compute attachments. We'll itemize that in the SOW.

Action items from Redwoods: 
- Priyom — can you run a quick unit-cost calc for 100M vs 300M with the details Alex sent (avg seq length ~ ?). If we don’t have avg seq length, use 64 tokens/request baseline and show sensitivity.
- Marissa — I’ll need you to prepare a draft SOW + pricing sheet to share on Monday.

Alex — I’ve calendared Mon 10/05 10:00am PT. I’ll send an invite with a short agenda (walk pricing, licensing approaches, and support terms).

Best — Ben

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Private/VPC pricing - unit economics notes (internal)

Internal notes for pricing draft (quick, rough):
- Assumptions: avg seq = 64 tokens/request; 80% prompt / 20% completion split; model footprint ~ 30B parameter class on customer infra (GPU profile: A100 equivalent).
- 100M tokens/month: ~1.6M requests/month at 64 tokens/request. Peak concurrency estimate: ~40 rps assuming steady distribution with bursts. 
- 300M tokens/month: ~4.8M requests/month; plan for 3x compute (or autoscale) — baseline reserved capacity equivalent to 3x compute nodes.
- Cost bands (very rough): committed throughput model: $/1M tokens = $550 @100M, $425 @300M (volume discount). License + per-instance: flat license $60k/mo + per-GPU runtime charges ~ $Xk/mo; add enterprise support 18-22% of license.
- Recommend we present both: committed tokens with tiered $/1M and license+compute with example runbook for environment counts.

I’ll produce a short tab in the draft pricing spreadsheet showing sensitivity to avg seq length (32/64/128).

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com

Note: numbers above are preliminary and will be refined once we ingest fintech token CSV.
